title: align-auth-ttl-heartbeat-and-stream-facade-across-sdks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Unify session TTL handling and streaming heartbeat across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; introduce compact stream facade UX and bump SDK versions (py 0.43.0, ts 1.12.0, go v1.5.2).
description: Context & motivation: Multiple SDK consumers reported subtle mismatches between server-side session TTL propagation, streaming heartbeats, and SDK-side retry/keepalive semantics. This caused short-lived production flakes where long-lived streaming clients were reauthorized unexpectedly or experienced silent stalls. This PR harmonizes the contract across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: 1) explicitly propagate server-issued session TTL to SDK session managers; 2) provide an optional lightweight heartbeat/ping helper on streaming handles to keep ephemeral sessions alive without user-managed timers; 3) expose a compact consumer-facing StreamFacade that simplifies reconnect + backoff + credential refresh for most application scenarios. Work items completed: - Add session TTL propagation path (server -> SDK session cache) - Implement StreamHeartbeat helper with jittered pings and backoff-aware suppression - Introduce StreamFacade in each SDK with ergonomic defaults (auto-reconnect, credential refresh hook, graceful drain) - Add deterministic retry presets for transient auth failures and integrate into facade - Add unit/integration tests across tri-SDK CI matrix - Bump SDK versions (python 0.43.0, typescript 1.12.0, go v1.5.2) Commits (high-level): - 3a7f8d2: session: surface server ttl in session envelope and client hints - 7b21c4a: sdk-common: introduce ttl-aware SessionManager and TTL expiry events - f4d0b9e: py-sdk: add StreamHeartbeat and StreamFacade; tests + docstrings - d12e6b1: ts-sdk: compact StreamFacade, heartbeat shim, export types - a9c6e3f: go-sdk: session TTL handling and lightweight facade implementation - c8b0d2f: tests: add e2e streaming fixture to exercise reauth and heartbeat - e1b3f75: docs: add stream-facade quickstart and migration notes Changed areas (high level): - sdk-common/session/* (new helper & interfaces) - python/redwood_sdk/streaming/facade.py (new) - typescript/packages/sdk/src/stream/facade.ts (new) - go/sdk/session/facade.go (new) - sdk-common/tests/* (new cross-sdk fixtures) - docs/quickstarts/stream-facade.md (new) - changelogs/* (version entries) Review conversation summary: - Priya requested clearer guarantees around TTL semantics: author added explicit contract notes and unit tests showing TTL extension vs. renewal semantics. - Liam flagged potential race in the Go facade's reconnect path where inflight token rotation could be dropped; addressed by serializing credential handoffs and adding a small integration test. - Diego found a lint failure in the TypeScript heartbeat jitter implementation; fix included to use crypto-safe jitter on Node/browser. - One CI run initially failed on ts lint and py flake; author pushed fixes and re-ran. Approvals: Priya Rao (approved after test additions), Diego Martínez (approved), Liam O'Connor (approved). CI: initial run: fail (ts lint, py flake); subsequent run: pass across linux/macos/windows tri-matrix. Migration notes & developer guidance: - New StreamFacade is opt-in; existing streaming APIs remain supported. - If you previously implemented custom heartbeat, consider switching to StreamHeartbeat for consistent jitter and suppression behavior. - Session TTL is now delivered via session.envelope.ttl_seconds; SDK session managers will emit TTL_EXPIRE events to allow graceful drain. Testing & observability: - Added new e2e fixture that simulates auth server issuing short TTLs and verifies StreamFacade reauth flow. - Instrumented metrics: sdk.session.ttl_updated, sdk.stream.heartbeat_sent, sdk.stream.reconnect_attempt. Risk & rollback: feature is guarded behind a facade and opt-in defaults; can be disabled by setting facade: { enabled: false } in SDK config. If a regression is found, revert commit f4d0b9e / d12e6b1 / a9c6e3f depending on language. Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Notes on uniqueness: This PR focuses on aligning server->SDK TTL semantics and introducing a minimal heartbeat helper plus an ergonomically opinionated StreamFacade that collapses several previous extension points into a single, well-tested entrypoint for most customers.
